kidb1.intro: The Classical, Mar del Plata: White closes the centre, the knight reroutes, and Black starts the pawn storm with the f-pawn.
notes: d4 takes space in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 brings the king's knight out so the centre can be challenged.
c4 fights for d5, so Black cannot easily put a pawn there.
g6 prepares the fianchetto. The dark-squared bishop wants the long diagonal.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight behind the pawn on c4, so it can support the pawn push to e4.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal. It will press down that diagonal once the knight on f6 moves.
e4 joins the pawns on c4 and d4 and opens the light-squared bishop.
d6 frees the light-squared bishop and prepares a pawn push to e5.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
O-O castles the king to g8 and the rook to f8, behind the fianchetto.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and clears the way to castle.
e5 attacks the pawn on d4. This is Black's challenge to the broad centre.
O-O castles the king to g1 and the rook to f1 before the centre closes.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
d5 attacks the knight on c6 and closes the centre. Play now has to happen on the wings.
Ne7 steps the knight off the attack from the pawn on d5. It can support a kingside pawn advance from here.
Ne1 steps the king's knight aside so the f-pawn can move. The knight can reroute from the back rank.
Nd7 defends the pawn on e5 and gets ready for a kingside pawn advance.
f3 defends the pawn on e4 and covers g4.
f5 attacks the pawn on e4 and starts the kingside pawn advance.

d5 attacks the knight on c6 and closes the centre. Play now has to happen on the wings.
Ne7 steps the knight off the attack from the pawn on d5. It can support a kingside pawn advance from here.
b4 gains queenside space and covers c5.
a5 attacks the pawn on b4 and challenges that advance.
bxa5 takes the pawn on a5. The queenside starts to open.
Rxa5 recaptures the pawn on a5. The rook lands on a half-open file.
a4 gains space and covers b5.
b6 defends the rook on a5 and covers c5.
Ba3 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on d6.
Nd7 defends the pawn on e5. White's knight on f3 is attacking that pawn.
Re1 gets ready for the light-squared bishop to drop back to f1. After that, the rook defends the pawn on e4.
f5 attacks the pawn on e4 and starts the kingside pawn advance.

kidb3.intro: The Petrosian: White plays a pawn to d5 and a bishop to g5, Black kicks that bishop with the h-pawn and the g-pawn, and the knight comes to h5.

Nf6 brings the king's knight out so the centre can be challenged.

e5 attacks the pawn on d4. This is Black's challenge to the broad centre.
O-O castles the king to g1 and the rook to f1 before the centre closes.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5, which the knight on f3 attacks.
d5 closes the centre and covers c6.
a5 gains space and covers b4.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
h6 attacks the dark-squared bishop and asks it to move.
Bh4 keeps the knight on f6 pinned to the queen on d8 and steps off the pawn on h6.
g5 attacks the bishop on h4. Black loosens the kingside to chase that bishop.
Bg3 steps off the pawn on g5 instead of taking it.
Nh5 attacks the bishop on g3 and offers the knight for that bishop.

Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the pawn on d4.
exd4 takes the pawn on d4 and leaves the e-file half-open for Black.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. A knight now sits in the centre.
Re8 puts the rook on the half-open e-file and attacks the pawn on e4.
f3 defends the pawn on e4.
c6 covers d5 and keeps the centre solid.

kidb5.intro: The Samisch: White plays the f-pawn, a bishop to e3 and the queen to d2, and Black expands on the queenside with the a-pawn and a rook to b8.
notes: d4 takes space in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 brings the king's knight out so the centre can be challenged.

f3 defends the pawn on e4 and covers g4.

Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the pawn on d4.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
Qd2 places the queen beside the bishop on e3. White can now castle queenside.
a6 covers b5, ready for a pawn advance there.
Nge2 develops the king's knight. The pawn on f3 has taken its usual square, so the knight uses e2.
Rb8 puts the rook on the b-file, ready to support a pawn advance there.

kidb6.intro: The Four Pawns Attack: White grabs space with the f- and d-pawns, and Black blows the centre open with pawn breaks.
notes: d4 takes space in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 brings the king's knight out so the centre can be challenged.
c4 fights for d5, so Black cannot easily put a pawn there.
g6 prepares the fianchetto. The dark-squared bishop wants the long diagonal.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight behind the pawn on c4, so it can support the pawn push to e4.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal. It will press down that diagonal once the knight on f6 moves.
e4 joins the pawns on c4 and d4 and opens the light-squared bishop.
d6 frees the light-squared bishop and prepares a pawn push to e5.
f4 grabs more space. That large centre will need looking after.
O-O castles the king to g8 and the rook to f8, behind the fianchetto.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and chips at the centre.
d5 gains a wedge of space in the centre.
e6 attacks the pawn on d5 and chips at that wedge.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and prepares castling.
exd5 takes the pawn on d5 and leaves the e-file half-open for Black.
cxd5 recaptures the pawn on d5. White keeps a pawn in the centre.
Re8 puts the rook on the half-open e-file and attacks the pawn on e4.
e5 advances, attacking the knight on f6 and the pawn on d6.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and leaves the d-file half-open for Black.

kidb7.intro: The Fianchetto: both bishops sit on the long diagonal, Black plays the queen's knight to d7 and a pawn to c6, and the centre is traded on d4.
notes: d4 takes space in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 brings the king's knight out so the centre can be challenged.
c4 fights for d5, so Black cannot easily put a pawn there.
g6 prepares the fianchetto. The dark-squared bishop wants the long diagonal.
g3 prepares White's own fianchetto. White is not building the broad pawn centre yet.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal. It will press down that diagonal once the knight on f6 moves.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal against Black's queenside and gets White ready to castle.
O-O castles the king to g8 and the rook to f8, behind the fianchetto.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
d6 frees the light-squared bishop and prepares a pawn push to e5.
O-O castles the king to g1 and the rook to f1, behind the fianchetto.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and leaves the c-pawn free to move.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight behind the pawn on c4, so it can support the pawn push to e4.
e5 attacks the pawn on d4.
e4 builds the full pawn centre, so Black has to decide whether to take on d4.
c6 covers d5 and keeps the centre solid.
h3 covers g4 and gives the king on g1 a little air.
Re8 puts the rook on the e-file and defends the pawn on e5.
Re1 puts the rook on the e-file and defends the pawn on e4.
exd4 takes the pawn on d4 and leaves the e-file half-open for Black.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight replaces the pawn in the centre.

kidb8.intro: The Averbakh: the bishop comes to g5 and then f4, and Black challenges the centre with the c-pawn and the e-pawn.
notes: d4 takes space in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 brings the king's knight out so the centre can be challenged.
c4 fights for d5, so Black cannot easily put a pawn there.

e4 joins the pawns on c4 and d4 and opens the light-squared bishop.
d6 frees the light-squared bishop and prepares a pawn push to e5.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and keeps g5 free for the dark-squared bishop.
O-O castles the king to g8 and the rook to f8, behind the fianchetto.
Bg5 attacks the knight on f6. The pawn on e7 keeps the queen on d8 off that diagonal, so the knight is not pinned.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and challenges the centre.
d5 gains a wedge of space in the centre.
h6 attacks the bishop on g5.
Bf4 steps off the pawn on h6 and attacks the pawn on d6.
e6 attacks the pawn on d5 and chips at the wedge.

kidb9.intro: The Exchange: the centre comes off, the queens are traded, and both sides bring out the remaining pieces.
notes: d4 takes space in the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 brings the king's knight out so the centre can be challenged.
c4 fights for d5, so Black cannot easily put a pawn there.

dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and leaves the d-file half-open for White.
dxe5 recaptures the pawn on e5 and keeps a black pawn there, so the queens can come off on the open d-file.
Qxd8 takes the queen on d8. Only the rook on f8 can take it back, with the knight on b8 blocking the rook on a8.
Rxd8 recaptures the queen on d8. The rook takes the open file while White's king is still on e1.
O-O gets the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps away from the open d-file.
c6 covers d5, so a knight cannot settle there.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and covers c5.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the pawn on e5, which the knight on f3 attacks.
